data.name: Netflix
data.notes:
###Why Traceroute Will Mislead You###

Connectivity to www.netflix.com is not indicative of connectivity to the Netflix content delivery service. Webpages on netflix.com are often served from AWS in the US and Ireland. The best method to investigate reachability is to expand the AS-NFLX IRR object and review those prefixes or alternatively contact our NOC email address for assistance.

###Peering in Brazil (PTT)###

A Netflix (ASN 2906) está no ATM do [IX.BR](http://ix.br) das cidades de São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Porto Alegre e Fortaleza. Temos uma política aberta de peering, anunciando todas as nossas rotas para os route servers (ATM) desta localidades. Anunciamos um pequeno número de prefixos e não existe diferenças entre os prefixos anunciados para os servidores de rota (route servers) e sessões bi-laterais.

Se você é um novo membro no [IX.BR](http://ix.br), visite a [página de participantes](http://ix.br/particip/sp) e verifique os que possuem a designação de ATM. Isso significa que você já começa trocar tráfego com todos eles com uma única configuração com os route servers. A Netflix prefere as sessões de peering com os route servers do que estabelecer sessões bi-laterais para facilitar e agilizar as ativações. Também recomendamos que os participantes criem registros no [https://www.peeringdb.com](https://www.peeringdb.com) para fornecer visibilidade da suas redes e suas políticas de roteamento.

###MEDs###

We accept MEDs within a relevant geographical area (example: we will not serve UK content from Atlanta), but we automatically add a MED of 50 to PNI and 100 to IX in addition to the MED you send us. We use MEDs BEFORE geolocation - they will always override our geolocation service. Note that you will only receive prefixes relevant to the region that you interconnect.

### Geolocation and Proxy Blocking support ###
For support with geolocation and proxy blocking issues, open a request [here]( https://openconnect.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=43998445522957)

###AS40027 Assistance###

The email addresses in our AS2906 record cannot assist with connections from AS40027. For concerns with AS40027, please utilize our [partner portal](https://openconnect.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001068512-Getting-started-with-Partner-Portal#h_01G7T67328ABT7X95V6MPP626A) to connect with the right team.

###Additional Information###

Additional information about Open Connect, the Netflix CDN project, is available at [https://openconnect.netflix.com](https://openconnect.netflix.com)

data.notes:
## AWS Peering - [https://peering.aws/](https://peering.aws/)

### Peering requests

#### IX
- Please use our peering portal to request IX peering sessions: [https://interconnect.amazon/](https://interconnect.amazon/) 

- *Note: If you're about to request IX peering sessions with AS16509 and currently do NOT have any peering with AS16509 established, please reach out to the regional contacts below.*

#### PNI
- AWS prefers 400GE, accepts 100GE and no longer supports 10GE PNIs.
When submitting a PNI peering request, please only address the specific regional contact listed below, related to the geographical region in which you wish to request PNI peering in.

- (Example: PNI peering requests for London should use peering-emea@amazon.com while PNI peering requests for Singapore should use peering-apac@amazon.com). 

- This will ensure your request is processed and addressed in a timely fashion. Please do not copy contacts not meant for peering policy in the location of your request.

#### ACE
- For ACE Embed cache information & operational issues please use our ACE portal: [https://interconnect.amazon/epop](https://interconnect.amazon/epop)

#### RPKI
- AWS drops all routes identified as RPKI invalid on incoming eBGP sessions.

#### Informational
- For details about our network, routing and interconnection options, please see [https://peering.aws](https://peering.aws). 

- AWS IP ranges with source location information: [https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json](https://ip-ranges.amazonaws.com/ip-ranges.json). 

- Please use the Maintenance alias only to notify us regarding maintenance activities on your end and do not copy other aliases into these inquiries. 

### Operational issues
- If you experience connectivity issues to Amazon AS16509, please reach out to our Technical Operations contact below. When contacting please include the following info to reduce the troubleshooting time: 
```
- Short description of the observed problem and impact 
- SRC & DST IP address 
- BGP peer information 
- Traceroute or similar valuable debug output. 
```
- Please **DO NOT** contact policy addresses for operational support.

- EC2 Reachability Test available at: [http://ec2-reachability.amazonaws.com](http://ec2-reachability.amazonaws.com)

We may decide to only send our regional routes to an ISP where sending all of our routes may have a detrimental effect on the latency and routing of existing traffic. Our regions are Europe, Asia and America currently. Where we have low port speeds onto an exchange, we will happily peer with ISPs (and actively want to establish peers there) but we consider these backup routes so you may not see much traffic from us.

We recommend a max-prefix value of 500, and prefer md5 passwords on sessions.

We usually will accept private peering requests for peers where we exchange 75Mbps or more. PNIs must be a minimum of 1Gbps and we aim to start looking at upgrading capacity once a PNI regularly exceeds 50%

Most of our traffic is IPTV from multiple popular services, if you'd like to discuss us sending our traffic to you via alternative routes then please get in touch with our Support contact.

data.name: Equinix Internet Exchange - MLPE Route Servers
data.name_long: Multi-Lateral Peering Exchange, IX  route server peering
data.notes:
The Equinix MLPE service automates peering for open networks by providing route servers for participants to exchange routing information with multiple peers using only a pair of BGP sessions. 

This allows for the establishment of sessions without a bilateral peering agreement in place with the participating networks, The MLPE route server peering is available at all Equinix Internet Exchange locations.  

All Equinix MLPE route servers support the ability for participants to more granularly control outbound announcements of their routes using BGP Communities:

[MLPE BGP Communities info] (https://docs.equinix.com/en-us/Content/Interconnection/IX/IX-mlpe-bgp-communities.htm)

Please note that despite the unified ASN, the Equinix MLPE service does not redistribute prefixes between Internet Exchanges in different metros.

IX participants can subscribe to the MLPE  route server peering using the IX Portal. 

[ix.equinix.com/ixp/mlpeRegistration] (https://ix.equinix.com/ixp/mlpeRegistration)

data.name: Brennercom
data.notes:
We have a selective peering policy and evaluate each request based on its merits. We also require from our peers:

* common sense
* must filter customer prefixes strictly
* must not leak prefixes from non-customer sessions (even if the prefix is from a customer)
* an updated peeringdb entry
* reasonable prefix aggregation
* responsive NOC
* peers IX-link must not be congested
* IPv6 peering, if peer AS is v6 enabled
* must not be our customer, or a customer of a existing peer
* do not send automated emails to our NOC for whatever reason; humans only!

Peering through route servers is usually preferred over dedicated BGP sessions, especially for low-volume, low-prefix peers that are already connected to the route servers. This is to avoid unnecessary maintenance and configuration overhead.

We filter all our customers with strict prefix-lists (along with other industry standard filtering and security measures), no exceptions.

Peering and embedded cache guidelines available at [cloudflare.com/peering-policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/peering-policy/).

data.name: Cisco Systems, Inc.
data.notes:
Overview:
Cisco Systems (AS109) provides connectivity for Cisco's corporate network and cisco.com based Internet services.  Cisco is actively expanding its peering footprint globally across Europe, North America, and Asia Pacific.  At this time a selective peering policy has been chosen where Cisco will limit the number of bilateral peers. Cisco will not be peering through exchange route servers.

General Terms:
* Peering agreements will be reviewed yearly to ensure traffic requirements are maintained.
* Cisco reserves the right to modify this policy at any time without notice.  
* Compliance with the terms of this policy does not guarantee a peering relationship with Cisco.  This policy is a guideline and Cisco may refuse peering for any reason without disclosure.
* Peering may be temporarily or permanently disconnected by either party for any reason.
* Cisco and Requester agree not to abuse the peering relationship.  Examples of abusive behavior are, but are not limited to: static routes, default routes, improper filtering,  and willfully sending malicious traffic.

Guidelines and Requirements:
* Cisco shall maintain accurate contact information and POP presence at peeringdb.com.
* Both IPv4 and IPv6 peering is preferred at all exchanges.
* Cisco advertises regional prefixes in each exchange location and will not provide consistent advertisements across regions.
* Cisco does not expect consistent advertisements from peers.
* Cisco (AS109) will only accept and advertise prefixes for AS109 and will not act as transit for any other ASNs.
* Requester must be connected to an Internet Exchange where Cisco (AS109) presently peers as listed on peeringdb.com.
* Requester must operate a 24x7 Network Operation Center and must respond to all reported issues within 24 hours.
* Requester must maintain a peeringdb.com record with accurate contact information and public peering exchange point details.
	

Requesting Peering:
All requests which meet the guidelines and requirements must be e-mailed to as109-peering@cisco.com and must contain the following information:
* Requester's ASN and all proposed ASNs to be advertised.
* List of common interconnection points.
* Ingress and egress bitrates, based upon 95th percentile, per requested exchange points over prior 90 days.
* Maximum number of prefixes expected to be advertised.
* Description of type of traffic carried by requester's network.
* Authentication support

Requests which meet the minimum requirements for peering will be reviewed. If approved, Cisco will contact you. Unfortunately, due to the number of requests we receive, we may not be able to respond to all requests.

# DE-CIX Hamburg Route Servers

## Route Server Address Information

**rs1.ham.de-cix.net**

**rs2.ham.de-cix.net**

---

## Route Server Control

You may use BGP Standard or Large Communities to control route redistribution via the route servers:

* **(43252:43252), (43252:1:0):** Redistribute to all route server peers (default)

* **(43252:<peer ASN>), (43252:1:<peer ASN>):** Redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:<peer ASN>), (43252:0:<peer ASN>):** Do not redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:43252), (43252:0:0):** Do not redistribute

If <peer ASN> uses a 16b ASN, you may use BGP Standard or Large Communities

If <peer ASN> uses a 32b ASN, you have to use BGP Large Communities

There are additional communities for controlling announcements:

* **65535:0**           GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN
* **65535:666**       BLACKHOLE
* **43252:65281**   NO_EXPORT
* **43252:65282**   NO_ADVERTISE

---

## Additional Information

For more information on route server control and Blackholing, please see:

[DE-CIX Hamburg Route Server Guide](https://docs.de-cix.net/article/zzj4c9g352)

[DE-CIX Blackholing Guide](https://docs.de-cix.net/category/yj9onxuefs)

data.name: NIC.br - SIMET
data.notes: SIMET  (Traffic Measurement System) - http://simet.nic.br/ which consists of a webpage with a Java applet and servers inside our Internet Exchange Points. The Java applet can measure delay, jitter, TCP and UDP bandwidth, among other network parameters. There are a lot of such tests spread over the Internet, but ours has two important characteristics that bring some advantages. First: the majority of Brazilian Internet providers exchange traffic directly with the network in which SIMET servers are; it is almost the same as to have the test servers inside the provider network, the results are not distorted by foreign networks. Second: alongside with giving the end user the knowledge about the quality of his connection, we collect the data, and it becomes an important tool for the Brazilian Internet Steering Comittee to know the general quality of our national Internet Providers.

All networks are requested to keep their PeeringDB record accurate and up-to-date.

General Peering Requirements

All potential peering partners must meet the following criteria:
 - Operate a 24x7 NOC that is responsive to operational and security issues.
 - Maintain an accurate and complete PeeringDB entry, including NOC contact details and listed interconnection facilities.
 - Maintain accurate route objects in a major Internet Routing Registry (IRR), such as RADb or ARIN. We will use this information to build prefix filters.
 - Maintain accurate RPKI records.
 - Must not point a default route or use static routes directed at our network for traffic that is not covered by the peering agreement.
 - Must only announce your own prefixes and those of your direct downstream customers. We will not accept announcements for prefixes belonging to your transit providers or other peers.
 - Must implement filtering to prevent the propagation of route leaks and bogon prefixes. We encourage the adoption of MANRS principles.
 - Must agree to collaboratively troubleshoot and resolve network issues, including routing anomalies, security events, and performance degradation.

Public Peering (Internet Exchange Points - IXPs)

We welcome peering over shared IXP fabrics where we have a mutual presence.
 - Locations: We are present at the following IXPs:
1. Equinix Dallas (DA3) 
2. Amarillo Petroleum Building
 - Requirements:
1. Both IPv4 and IPv6 sessions are required where available.
2. MD5 is not required but can be configured upon request.

Private Network Interconnect (PNI)
We will consider direct, private interconnections for networks that can exchange a significant volume of traffic with our network.
 - Locations: We can establish PNIs at the following data centers:
1. 203 SW 8th Ave Amarillo, TX
2. 1950 Stemmons Dallas, TX
3. 1220 Broadway Lubbock, TX
 - Requirements:
1. Peers are responsible for ordering and covering the costs of the physical cross-connect to our equipment in the mutual data center.
2. Link speeds supported are 10 Gbps and 100 Gbps.

Operational Policies
- Route Announcements: We will announce our aggregate prefixes and those of our downstream customers.
- Prefix Limits: We will set a maximum prefix limit based on the peer's IRR records. We request that peers do the same for our announcements. We will provide our suggested max-prefix value upon session establishment.
- Capacity Upgrades: We monitor all peering interface utilization. When an interface sustains traffic levels exceeding 75% for a 7-day period, we will initiate discussions with the peer to upgrade capacity. We expect our peers to have a similar policy.
- Maintenance: Scheduled maintenance will be announced at least 48 hours in advance via email to the peer's NOC contact. Emergency maintenance will be communicated as promptly as possible.

A Net&Com Internet possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

## Route Server Control

You may use BGP Standard or Large Communities to control route redistribution via the route servers:

* **(56890:56890), (56890:1:0):** Redistribute to all route server peers (default)

* **(56890:<peer ASN>), (56890:1:<peer ASN>):** Redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:<peer ASN>), (56890:0:<peer ASN>):** Do not redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:56890), (56890:0:0):** Do not redistribute

If <peer ASN> uses a 16b ASN, you may use BGP Standard or Large Communities

If <peer ASN> uses a 32b ASN, you have to use BGP Large Communities

data.name: Region Stockholm(RS)
data.notes:
Technical requirements:
Networks wishing to peer with SLL must have the following:

•Publicly routable ASN

•Publicly routable address space (at least one /24 of IPv4 and/or one /48 of IPv6 space)

•ASN record completed in PeeringDB

•Technical contact capable of resolving BGP routing issues

•Presence at Internet Exchange facilities listed for SLL in PeeringDB

•BGP MD5 password supported and preferred, not a requirement


Routing policy:
In general, SLL will advertise all SLL public routes over peering sessions with AS19399. No route of last resort (default route) will be advertised or directed at SLL.


Maximum prefixes:
SLL suggest peers set a max-prefix of 25 (IPv4) and 5 (IPv6) routes on peering sessions with SLL.


Routing announcements:
SLL asks that peers advertise all their public routes in all locations where they peer with SLL, unless an alternative route advertisement policy has been agreed. Routes should be aggregated as much as possible. No routes smaller than /25(IPv4) and /65(IPv6) will be accepted.

Stockholm County Council(SLL) is changing name to Region Stockholm(RS) in January 2019.

# DE-CIX Jakarta Route Servers

---

## Route Server Address Information

**rs1.jkt.de-cix.net**

* 2001:df5:7880::2614:a:1

**rs2.jkt.de-cix.net**

* 49.213.57.252
* 2001:df5:7880::2614:a:2

---

## Route Server Control

You may use BGP Standard or Large Communities to control route redistribution via the route servers:

* **(9748:9748), (9748:1:0):** Redistribute to all route server peers (default)

* **(9748:<peer ASN>), (9748:1:<peer ASN>):** Redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:<peer ASN>), (9748:0:<peer ASN>):** Do not redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:9748), (9748:0:0):** Do not redistribute

If <peer ASN> uses a 16b ASN, you may use BGP Standard or Large Communities

If <peer ASN> uses a 32b ASN, you have to use BGP Large Communities

There are additional communities for controlling announcements:

* **65535:0**           GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN
* **65535:666**       BLACKHOLE
* **9748:65281**   NO_EXPORT
* **9748:65282**   NO_ADVERTISE

---

## Additional Information

For more information on route server control and Blackholing, please see:

data.name: Adminor Aktiebolag
data.notes:
## Adminor AB — AS51701

Adminor is a Swedish network operator and hosting provider based in Stockholm. We offer co-location, VPS, dedicated servers and more in our facilities.
We operate our own AS with IPv4 and IPv6 transit and peering.

### Peering Policy
Open peering policy. We welcome peering with networks of all sizes.
Peering requests can be sent to noc@adminor.net.

### Technical Requirements
- Routeable prefix minimum: /24 (IPv4), /48 (IPv6)
- No-export and blackhole communities honored
- RPKI/ROV enforced — INVALID routes are rejected
- We do not accept default routes
- We do not accept bogons or our own prefixes

### Transit Providers
- Portlane / Glesys (AS42708)
- Layermesh

### IXP Presence
- SONIX (Stockholm)

### Facility Presence
- KN7, Stockholm
- VästbergaDC, Stockholm
- SolnaB15, Solna

### BGP Communities
We support BGP communities for traffic engineering (prepend, no-export)
toward specific peers and transit providers. Contact NOC for details.

### Contact
NOC: noc@adminor.net
Peering: noc@adminor.net

data.name: BALT-IX Route Servers
data.notes:
#  BGP Community routing:
Each of route-server does not modify, process or remove communities received from customers except those communities which are processed by the route-servers themselves:
   
//---  Communities affecting announces to other peers:  
0:8486       - Do not announce prefix to all peers.  
0:X          - Do not announce prefix to peer ASX.  
8486:8486    - Announce prefix to all peers.  
8486:X       - Announce prefix to peer ASX only.  

If peer's AS is 32-bit then BGP extended community attribute should be used:   
rt:0:X       - Do not announce prefix to peer ASX  
rt:8486:X    - Announce prefix to peer ASX only  
   

RS doesn't insert its own ASN into the AS_PATH by default, some routers might deny such updates, to solve this behavior you should specify "no bgp enforce-first-as" (IOS/IOS-XE).

# **SAIX Saudi Arabia Route Servers**
SAIX operates two Route-Servers and It is advised to peer with both.

## **Route Server Address Information**
**RIX-RS1**
- 45.94.12.5
- 2001:1497::5

**RIX-RS2**

## **Route Server Control**
### **BGP Operational Communities:**
You have to use BGP Community to control route advertisement for dynamic filtering via the Route-Servers:
**SAIX support either BGP Standard-Community or Large-Community or combination of them**

- **Standard or Large Community (20759:20759) or (20759:1:0):**

 Route-Servers redistribute your prefixes to all (other) peers

- **Standard or Large Community (0:20759) or (20759:0:0):**
 
 Route-Servers wouldn’t redistribute your prefixes to any peer

- **Standard or Large Community (20759:20759) (0:PEER-AS1) (0:PEER-AS2) or (20759:1:0) (20759:0:PEER-AS1) (20759:0:PEER-AS2):**
 
 Route-Servers redistribute your prefixes to all (other) peers except PEER-AS1&PEER-AS2

- **Standard or Large Community (0:20759) (20759:PEER-AS1) (20759:PEER-AS2) or (20759:0:0) (20759:1:PEER-AS1) (20759:1:PEER-AS2):**

 Route-Servers redistribute your prefixes only to PEER-AS1&PEER-AS2

- **Standard and Large Community (20759:20759) (0:PEER-AS1) (20759:0:PEER-AS2):**

 Route-Servers redistribute your prefixes to all (other) peers except PEER-AS1&PEER-AS2

For IX Peering:

* We generally peer with the route servers.

* We may withdraw any routes at any time without any notice.

For PNI:
* We may withdraw any routes at any time without any notice.
- We are slowly transitioning to a v6 only core; and would prefer that you engage with us with RFC5549 capable routers as we don't have address space to spare for PNI links (or provide your own v4 for PNI).
- We require at least two links for peering in a specific site. 
- Only multiple 100G supported for PNI, although we'll establish private peering at 2G in facilities with NRC-only or otherwise low XC fees (Nikhef, Halsey, certain other EU-region facilities).  Minimums elsewhere are roughly ~20G, although exceptions can be made.  

Optics supported for PNI:
- 100G-LR4

- 100G BIDI LR (1271nm/1331nm)

We aim to split an equal amount of costs.

A BrasilFone possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas. • O MD5 não é necessário

data.name: DE-CIX Lisbon Route Servers
data.notes:
# DE-CIX Lisbon Route Servers

---

## Route Server Address Information

**rs1.lis.de-cix.net**

* 185.1.131.252
* 2001:7f8:d5::aad1:fc:1

**rs2.lis.de-cix.net**

* 185.1.131.253
* 2001:7f8:d5::aad1:fd:1

---

## Route Server Control

You may use BGP Standard or Large Communities to control route redistribution via the route servers:

* **(43729:43729), (43729:1:0):** Redistribute to all route server peers (default)

* **(43729:<peer ASN>), (43729:1:<peer ASN>):** Redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:<peer ASN>), (43729:0:<peer ASN>):** Do not redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:43729), (43729:0:0):** Do not redistribute

If <peer ASN> uses a 16b ASN, you may use BGP Standard or Large Communities

If <peer ASN> uses a 32b ASN, you have to use BGP Large Communities

There are additional communities for controlling announcements:

* **65535:0**           GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN
* **65535:666**       BLACKHOLE
* **43729:65281**   NO_EXPORT
* **43729:65282**   NO_ADVERTISE

---

## Additional Information

For more information on route server control and Blackholing, please see:

[DE-CIX Lisbon Route Server Guide](https://docs.de-cix.net/article/eby0hvz0gx)

[DE-CIX Blackholing Guide](https://docs.de-cix.net/category/yj9onxuefs)

[DE-CIX Route Server Informational BGP Communities](https://docs.de-cix.net/article/oqsxcr457r)

[DE-CIX Route Server Action BGP Communities](https://docs.de-cix.net/article/fh5syii5dk)

data.name: jm telecomunicação e man.
data.notes:
A jm telecomunicação e man. ltda me . possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

Fiber Telecom (FT)
data.notes:
## Our network highlights
.

* AS41327 is matching **RPKI** validation state and rejects invalids 'invalid == reject' (since March 2019)

* AS41327 accepts & honors community 65535:0 **GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN** according to  [RFC8326](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc8326 "RFC8326 Doc")

* AS41327 accepts requests & encourages using 
BGP TTL security **GTSM** on peering sessions according to [RFC5082](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5082 "RFC5082 Doc")

* AS41327 accepts and configures **TCP-MD5** or **TCP-AO** (since January 2022) and/or **BFD** on BGP sessions, if requested

* AS41327 infrastructure is compliant with [**MANRS**](https://www.manrs.org/isps/participants/?gv_search=41327&mode=any) security indications

* AS41327 will announcing never via route servers in Italy

* Our network hosts also a **RIPE's K-Root** replica at Palermo (ns1.it-pmo.k.ripe.net) and a [**RIPE's Atlas Anchors**](https://atlas.ripe.net/probes/6762/) (it-pmo-as41327)

* MIX-IT router locations: Carini (PA), Milan and Rome

* NetIX router locations: Milan and Frankfurt

* DE-CIX Dusseldorf, Hamburg, Madrid, Marseille, Munich, New York, MSK-IX and NYIIX are backhauled to Frankfurt, Germany

* France-IX AURA is temporary backhauled to Turin, Italy

* LSIX, DATAIX and Global-IX are backhauled to Amsterdam, Netherlands 

* France-IX is backhauled to Cornaredo (MI), Italy

* LINX is backhauled to Frankfurt, Germany

* Namex Bari is backhauled to Rome, Italy

* We can evaluate PNIs request with minimum 1Gbps traffic in any direction

data.notes:
A PC CONNECT TELECOM LTDA possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

* **(56858:56858), (56858:1:0):** Redistribute to all route server peers (default)

* **(56858:<peer ASN>), (56858:1:<peer ASN>):** Redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:<peer ASN>), (56858:0:<peer ASN>):** Do not redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:56858), (56858:0:0):** Do not redistribute

If <peer ASN> uses a 16b ASN, you may use BGP Standard or Large Communities

If <peer ASN> uses a 32b ASN, you have to use BGP Large Communities

data.name: BGP.Tools Route Collector
data.notes:
This is the route collector AS for bgp.tools. It does not carry traffic (apart from rare situations where it sends a single IPv6 prefix to a route server for backup reach-ability) on it's BGP sessions.

When peering with bgp.tools AS212232 you should export a full table (1M routes IPv4, 200k routes IPv6) like you would export to a potential customer. 

If you do not then bgp.tools will not be able to calculate your network statistics and the sessions may be removed to recover capacity. There are certain situations where internal resource shortages may mean not all prefixes are accepted/imported, but please export the full table regardless so this can be dynamically managed on our end!

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

data.name: RTIX Route Servers
data.notes:
To join in RTIX write to **help@ria.ee**

# Community based prefix filtering

The RTIX route server system also provides well known communities to allow members to control the distribution of their prefixes.

These communities are defined as follows:

- Prevent announcement of a prefix to a peer: **0:peer-as**
- Announce a route to a certain peer: **1:peer-as**
- Prevent announcement of a prefix to all peers: **0:0**
- Announce a route to all peers: **1:1**

To instruct the route servers to distribute a particular prefix only to AS64111 and AS64222, the prefix should be tagged with communities: **0:0**, **1:64111** and **1:64222**

Alternatively, to announce a prefix to all RTIX members, excluding AS64333, the prefix should be tagged with community **0:64333**. 

The RTIX route server supports BGP large community prefix distribution control, using the following policy:

- Prevent announcement of a prefix to a peer: **207800:0:peer-as**
- Announce a route to a certain peer: **207800:1:peer-as**
- Prevent announcement of a prefix to all peers: **207800:0:0**
- Announce a route to all peers: **207800:1:1**

## Filtering Policy 
1. Drop all well-known martians and bogons. 
2. Ensure that the peer AS is the same as the first AS in the AS path. 
3. Drop any prefix with a transit network ASN in the AS path. 
4. If the prefix is evaluated as RPKI valid, accept. 
5. If the prefix is evaluated as RPKI invalid, drop.

data.name: Novecore
data.notes:
Novecore selectively directs users' upload and websocket traffic to this network if it determines the user's ISP has routing deficiencies, such as packet loss or unusually high latencies, to Cloudflare and Novecore's other network service providers.

While the vast majority of networks should not be seeing any traffic to or from this ASN, we recommend every eyeball ISP to peer with it as a precautionary measure so a direct connection to your network is available when needed. Even if your routing is normally excellent, temporary issues can always occur, which our system will automatically pick up and attempt to fix through re-routing.

This ASN will peer with networks who meet one or more of the following criteria:
- Is already being re-routed to this ASN (visit [test.r.novecore.com](https://test.r.novecore.com) to check)
- Is an eyeball ISP, or a NSP primarily serving eyeball ISPs

While we peer with the route servers of some IXPs, we restrict export and import of routes to networks meeting the peering requirements above.

Peers will further need to be able to guarantee that there will not be congestion between the peering point and its end-users.

Peering with this ASN does not guarantee that Novecore upload and websocket traffic is routed via peering as our system automatically optimizes routing for every individual user. Other traffic, such as Novecore's website itself, is currently never served via this network.

**If you are a Novecore licensee receiving content uploads from Novecore via Staclar EDP (direct DDEX integration), you will want to peer with AS34854 instead.**

data.name: Maharlika IX Route Servers
data.notes:
Maharlika IX (Maharlika Internet Exchange) is a neutral, Filipino-built Internet Exchange Point that serves the Philippines. Our mission is to make interconnection more affordable and accessible, bring content closer to local and underserved networks, and extend the exchange directly to member networks. Guided by the principles of makabayan and makamasa, we are committed to strengthening the nation's internet through better digital access for everyone.

Route Servers (AS9420)

  - RS1: 163.223.201.1 / 2001:df0:a940::9420:1
  - RS2: 163.223.201.2 / 2001:df0:a940::9420:2

We operate two independent route servers on separate platforms and software. Members are encouraged to peer with both servers using IPv4 and IPv6. Please note that the previous peering LAN (103.121.64.0/24, 2400:efa0::/64) will remain in service until the announced cut-off date.

Routing Security

  - Operated in accordance with the MANRS actions for Internet Exchanges (IXPs).
  - RPKI Route Origin Validation: RPKI-invalid routes will be rejected.
  - IRR Filtering: Based on each member's PeeringDB AS-SET (please ensure yours is current).
  - Bogon prefixes and bogon ASNs are rejected; per-session max-prefix limits are enforced.
  - Our route servers are transparent; AS9420 is not inserted into the AS path.

BGP Large Communities

  - 9420:0:<peer-as>: do not announce to <peer-as>
  - 9420:0:0: do not announce to any peer
  - 9420:1:<peer-as>: announce to <peer-as> (this can be combined with 9420:0:0)
  - 9420:1000:x / 9420:1001:x: informational (RPKI / IRR validation state)

Registries and Listings

  - AS9420 and the peering LAN are registered with APNIC.
  - Our listing can be found in the IXPDB (Internet Exchange Point Database), featuring live member data from our IX-F export.

Contact

## Route Server Address Information

---

## Route Server Control

You may use BGP Standard or Large Communities to control route redistribution via the route servers:

* **(65534:65534), (133086:1:0):** Redistribute to all route server peers (default)

* **(65534:<peer ASN>), (133086:1:<peer ASN>):** Redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:<peer ASN>), (133086:0:<peer ASN>):** Do not redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:65534), (133086:0:0):** Do not redistribute

If <peer ASN> uses a 16b ASN, you may use BGP Standard or Large Communities

If <peer ASN> uses a 32b ASN, you have to use BGP Large Communities

There are additional communities for controlling announcements:

* **65535:0**           GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN
* **65535:666**       BLACKHOLE
* **65534:65281**   NO_EXPORT
* **65534:65282**   NO_ADVERTISE

---

## Additional Information

For more information on route server control and Blackholing, please see:

[Penang IX Route Server Guide](https://docs.de-cix.net/article/osk9adhcrt)

Peering requests must **ONLY** be sent to our Policy contact, which is visible in PeeringDB to logged in users.

## Route Server Control

You may use BGP Standard or Large Communities to control route redistribution via the route servers:

* **(65534:65534), (140307:1:0):** Redistribute to all route server peers (default)

* **(65534:<peer ASN>), (140307:1:<peer ASN>):** Redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:<peer ASN>), (140307:0:<peer ASN>):** Do not redistribute to <peer ASN>

* **(0:65534), (140307:0:0):** Do not redistribute

If <peer ASN> uses a 16b ASN, you may use BGP Standard or Large Communities

If <peer ASN> uses a 32b ASN, you have to use BGP Large Communities

There are additional communities for controlling announcements:

* **65535:0**           GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN
* **65535:666**       BLACKHOLE
* **65534:65281**   NO_EXPORT
* **65534:65282**   NO_ADVERTISE

---

# Available Networks

# Service Description
Strict peering policies of some networks may include the disfavor of route server peering and/or strict requirements for bilateral peering via GlobePEER or VirtualPNI. As many networks are not eligible to set up a peering in this case, DE-CIX also offers additional routes of selected partner networks via GlobePEER through the DE-CIX Layer 3 Services ASN (AS214292).
DE-CIX will take care of managing all peering relationships with these partners (so you don't have to) and will make their routes available from AS214292 via the GlobePEER route service at many DE-CIX Exchanges.

Thus, you can maintain a peering relationship with these networks without directly interacting with them or having to fulfil their peering requirements. All this is handled by DE-CIX.

You can check the [DE-CIX Looking Glass](https://lg.de-cix.net/search/?q=DE-CIX+Layer+3+Services) for additional routes that are currently being made available.

data.notes:
_We are merging AS212263 & AS31595 into AS8801, please reach out to the team to update your records_ 

**Peering Policy**

Rocket Fibre welcomes peering with networks that share a mutual interest in improving performance, resilience, and efficiency across the Internet. Our peering policy is selectively open, with criteria based on technical capability, operational discipline, and traffic volume.

**Peering Overview**

We maintain a pragmatic and scalable approach to peering. Our policy supports both public and private peering, depending on the level of traffic and strategic alignment.

**Traffic-Based Guidelines**

 - < 500 Mbps (95th percentile):
Please peer via route servers at a common public IXP.
 - 500 Mbps – 1 Gbps:
Direct bilateral BGP sessions may be established at a shared public IXP.
 - > 1 Gbps:
Private Network Interconnects (PNIs) will be considered at mutually available POPs.
  - > 10 Gbps:
If we do not currently share a common location, please reach out to discuss tailored interconnection options.

**Physical Interconnect Standards**

We support 
 - 10GE
 - 25G
 - 100GE
 - 400G interfaces 
only, or multiples thereof.

All interconnections must be over optical fiber using standard Ethernet handoffs (LR preferred).


**Technical Requirements**

 - To ensure operational stability and routing integrity, peers must:
 - Operate a publicly routed Autonomous System (ASN).
 - Not advertise prefixes more specific than /24 for IPv4 or /48 for IPv6.
 - Announce a consistent set of prefixes at all interconnection points, unless explicitly agreed otherwise.
 - Only send traffic destined for prefixes originated by Rocket Fibre.
 - Not send default routes or use static routing toward Rocket Fibre.
 - Maintain accurate IRR records (route/route6 objects) and filterable prefixes in a recognized IRR database.
 - Maintain a PeeringDB entry with up-to-date contact and network information.
 - Support BGP sessions with MD5 authentication if required.

**Operational Expectations**

 - We expect prompt response to operational issues and abuse complaints.
 - Peering links should be monitored, and sessions maintained in a clean, non-flapping state.
 - We reserve the right to temporarily or permanently disable any peering session that impacts our network stability.


**Multi-Exit Discriminators (MEDs)**

 - Not accepted by default.
 - If you intend to use MEDs for traffic engineering, please coordinate with us.

A Net&Com Internet possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

BGP Large Community Policy – Route Server AS154034

The route server (RS) recognizes and acts on the following large-community values.

General syntax:
154034:<action-code>:<peer-ASN>
Replace <peer-ASN> with the destination ASN (examples below use 65500 as a placeholder).

0 | Global Reject | Any prefix that carries 154034:0:0 is rejected. ---> 154034:0:0

0 | Per-Peer Reject | A prefix that carries 154034:0:<peer> is rejected only when exported to that specific peer ASN. ---> 154034:0:<Peer-AS>

1 | Announce a route to a certain peer | Allow the prefix to be advertised to a designated peer. ---> 154034:1:<Peer-AS>

101 | Prepend x1 | The RS prepends ASN 154034 once to the AS-PATH before sending the route to the peer. ---> 154034:101:<Peer-AS>

102	| Prepend x2 | The RS prepends ASN 154034 twice to the AS-PATH. ---> 154034:102:<Peer-AS>

103	| Prepend x3 | The RS prepends ASN 154034 three times to the AS-PATH. ---> 154034:103:<Peer-AS>

data.notes:
A new era of peering!

The future of peering on internet exchanges is under pressure, due to ever-growing costs, high number of failures, and a "too corporate" culture. In mid-2022 two internet pioneers decided to bring a better and more cost-effective alternative, and we never looked back.

### Our mission
It is our mission to redefine peering, by offering an innovative and cost-effective IXP ecosystem. The current state of peering is not-so-great and in a headlock by large corporate IXP-operators.

### Our way
We are truly neutral, fully privately owned and funded. Powered by a new generation of internet pioneers, our goal is to offer transparent and enterprise-ready connectivity services with a human touch.

### About us
We are the new-generation connectivity partner, fully privately owned and funded. We have built a next-generation connectivity fabric across major datacenters in Amsterdam and Frankfurt. [Read more](https://www.eranium.io/about) about our initiative.

### Latest news
Connect now with 400G! Read more about it on our [blog here](https://www.eranium.io/blog/114/the-new-fabric-and-400g).

data.name_long: Whisper Security (viaGraph B.V.) - verifiable agent identity on AS219419
data.notes:
AS219419 announces 2a04:2a01::/32 (WHISPER-AGENTS) and 2a04:2a00::/32 (WHISPER-INFRA).

The agent block is unusual and worth explaining: every address in it is a per-/128 assignment to a single AI agent or workload, each with its own reverse DNS, its own DANE-EE TLSA pin published in DNSSEC-signed DNS, and its own RDAP record. Anyone can verify any of it with stock tools and no account:

  dig +short -x <address>
  delv @1.1.1.1 -x <address>          re-derives the DNSSEC chain locally
  curl -s https://rdap.whisper.online/ip/<address>

Peering: open policy, IPv6-only, transit-only today. We drop RPKI-invalids. Max-prefix 2.
Looking glass (RFC 8522, machine-readable JSON): https://whisper.online/.well-known/looking-glass/v1

data.name: TekSavvy Solutions Inc.
data.notes:
Settlement-Free AS Interconnection Policy (AS5645)
--------------------------------------------------

We place a special emphasis on ensuring in-country interconnection for Canada-to-Canada traffic, and are present at all major Canadian and certain international peering points: please see PeeringDB for the current list.

[ROUTING]

1. VOLUME: For "international" peerings, the peer's peak AS-wide in or outbound traffic must exceed 10 Mbps.

International peerings are those occurring (a) exclusively through one or more interconnects outside Canada, or (b) within Canada, if the peer AS is mostly located outside Canada and cannot provide geographically diverse peering within Canada.

2. COMMON POINTS: Peering shall occur at all common public exchanges.

3. GLOBALLY CONSISTENT: Peers must maintain consistent route announcements at all interconnections.

4. IPv4-IPv6: Peering shall occur over IPv4 and IPv6 wherever both are available.

5. PEERING ISN'T TRANSIT: Peers may only send us traffic destined for the prefixes we announce to them.  They must not point default at us, establish a static route, reset next-hop, sell or give the next hop to third parties, or otherwise use a peering session for traffic whose origin or destination is a third-party AS.

[OPERATIONS]

6. NOC: Peers must operate a Network Operations Centre that is staffed and reachable 24/7, and has a timely escalation path to a clueful engineer.

7. CONTACTS: Peers must be listed and maintain updated contact information on PeeringDB.

8. SECURITY: Peers must work, and cooperate, to timely restrict denial of service attacks, unsolicited bulk email, damaged peering, and other network issues.

[TERMS]

9. PEERS AREN'T CUSTOMERS: Networks that have been, or have been downstream from, a TekSavvy transit customer within the preceding six months, are not eligible for peering.

10. CASE-BY-CASE: This policy sets out TekSavvy's policy for settlement-free AS interconnection. It is not a guarantee, and other factors could come into play -- TekSavvy reserves the right to peer with anyone we choose.

11. MAY CHANGE: Market and traffic conditions change. So does our business. TekSavvy may modify this policy at any time.

data.name: NORDUnet
data.aka: Nordic Gateway for Research and Education.
data.notes:
NORDUnet is a not-for-profit research and education network serving all research and higher education institutions in the Nordic countries, The Baltics, Poland, The Netherlands and Russia. Peering with NORDUnet provides connectivity to all researchers, students and educational institutions in these countries.

NORDUnet only serves the international academic community and does not provide connectivity or services to commercial networks.

We do require a updated PeeringDB-entry to be eligble to peer with NORDUnet. All peering is automated and is continuously monitored with the support of the data in PeeringDB. 

We also do require that the peering-partner peers with both IPv4 and IPv6.

We do honor GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN community 65535:0 on all eBGP-peering sessions which will set the received route on local-preference 0. 

We will perform latency-tests towards every peer to figure whether or not this is a local or remote-connection. We very rarely peer with remote and/or participants stretched beyond a metro-connection to the exchange.

We assume that everyone we peer with updates their IRR-record continuously since we do filtering on all inbound sessions with us based upon the data in the IRR dataset. We reserve the right to de-peer anyone that do not filter their own customers and do not honor BCP38 or in any other way misbehaves the built-in trust we have of operating BGP in the Default Free Zone.

RPKI:
NORDUnet drops all routes identified as RPKI invalid on incoming eBGP sessions.

We have a generally open [peering policy](http://as42695.net/peering-policy.txt), but will not peer with transit customers or their customers.

If you are also a participant, you can use our nodes for troubleshooting.
* Our [RIPE Atlas probes](https://atlas.ripe.net/probes/public?is_public=true&toggle=public&status=1&search=AS42695) might also be helpful for the same purpose.

data.name: REYVI INTERNET LTDA
data.notes:
REYVI INTERNET LTDA possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

## Route Server Control

You may use BGP Standard to control route redistribution via the route servers:

###Traffic management communities

Do not announce prefix to:
- **0:<peer-as>** - a peer with AS <peer-as>
- **0:<city-community>** - a peers with <city-community>
- **0:<segment-community>** - a peers with <segment-community>
- **0:50952** - anyone
- **0:666** - Blackhole community (/32 prefixes only)

Announce prefix to:
- **50952:<peer-as>** - a peer with AS <peer-as>
- **50952:50952** - everyone (default)

Local preference:
- **50952:0** - Set local preference 0
- **50952:50** - Set local preference 50
- **50952:80** - Set local preference 80

###Traffic management large communities

Do not announce prefix to:
- **50952:0:<peer-as>** - a peer with AS <peer-as>
- **50952:0:50952** - anyone

Announce prefix to:
- **50952:1:<peer-as>** - a peer with AS <peer-as>

-----

**Additional Information**

[management communities](https://apps.db.ripe.net/db-web-ui/query?from=www&searchtext=AS50952)

Tvrtka Pro-Ping osnovana je 2010. godine i jedna je od brzo rastućih komunikacijskih tvrtki na hrvatskom tržištu za prodaju, savjetovanje i izgradnju visokokvalitetnih komunikacijskih rješenja. Pro-PING vam može ponuditi cjelovita komunikacijska rješenja po principu 'ključ u ruke'.

Osnovne djelatnosti tvrtke su:

*Usluge savjetovanja i projektiranja mreža
*Nabava, izgradnja i održavanje mreže
*Bežična, optička i bakrena infrastuktura
*Zastupnici MikroTik sustava i opreme

*Mali, srednji i veliki korisnici

Početkom 2011. godine Pro-PING postaje Internet Service Provider, sa najpovoljnijom širokopojasnom Internet vezom za poslovne i privatne korisnike, baziranog na vlastitoj bežičnoj i optičkoj mrežnoj infrastrukturi.

Strategijom poslovanja usmjerenom na potrebe svih korisnika, pa i onih u ruralnim područjima, te pružanjem visoko kvalitetnih usluga, u mogućnosti smo ponuditi uslugu kvalitetne, brze i stabilne Internet veze. data.notes:
We have a selective but generally open peering policy and evaluate each request based on its value for our network.

Peering through route servers is usually preferred over direct BGP sessions, especially for low-volume, low-prefix peers that already use the route servers.
This is to avoid unnecessary maintenance and configuration overhead.
For direct BGP sessions we require a significant amount of traffic coming from or destined to your network.

Also an up-to-date PeeringDB entry is required for all public peering requests.

PNIs are preferred for peers with 95/5 > 3 Gbps.

* We filter all our customers with strict prefix-lists, no exceptions.
* We filter RPKI invalids on all sessions.
* We filter TIER1 ASNs in path on all peering + customer sessions.
* We do not accept prefixes smaller than /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6).

Additional BCP filtering as strictly as possible and other security measures are implied.

Please review your registered ROAs to reduce number of invalid prefixes.

data.name: CXC Route Servers
data.name_long: Multi-Lateral Peering Exchange, IX route server peering
data.notes:
The CXC-IX Multi-Lateral Peering Exchange (MLPE) streamlines the process of establishing peering connections across open networks. By leveraging our MLPE route servers, participants can connect with multiple peers through just two BGP sessions — eliminating the need for individual peering arrangements.

This service enables networks to exchange routing information without requiring direct bilateral agreements with other members. MLPE is available across all CXC-IX locations.

Participants also benefit from advanced route control through BGP Communities, allowing them to manage how their prefixes are shared on a per-peer basis.

[MPLE BGP Communities info](https://cloudxchange.id/rs)

**Important Note:**

Although CXC-IX uses a unified ASN for MLPE, routes are not propagated between different metropolitan areas.

A FIRENET SERVIÇOS DE TELECOMUNICAÇÕES LTDA possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

data.notes:
## Policy
Woodside operates AS38327 with a selective peering policy.

We will consider establishing peering to networks with which we exchange significant volumes of traffic, or those with whom we have another existing business relationship.

We are present on route servers in most locations but will otherwise seek bi-laterals via a common IX or direct PNIs where available and suitable.

Woodside also operates [AS400608](https://www.peeringdb.com/asn/400608) in North America.

---

## Requirements
All peers must have an up-to-date PeeringDB entry, including current exchange points with properly formatted public fabric addresses, prefix limits, and NOC contact information. 

Each entry must include an IRR as-set or route-set and should specify the source routing registry for that set. 

We prefer redundant connectivity in each location, delivered as dual PNIs or dual sessions over an IX.

---

## Contacts

Woodside provides contacts aligned to the [Contact Roles Glossary](https://docs.peeringdb.com/glossary/#contact-role-types).

Peering requests must **ONLY** be sent to our Policy contact, which is visible in PeeringDB to logged in users. 

Our maintenance contact should only be used to communicate outage notifications, and scheduling can be coordinated with our NOC where required.

data.name: ZANOG
data.notes:
We require peers to have a peering db entry and adequately maintain the entry to reflect current information.

We expect peers to provide us contact details via Peeringdb (either telephonic or email based) where we can address peering related issues. Such contact points should be monitored and responded to in a timely fashion.

We ask our peers to reciprocate with shortest exit (‘hot potato’) routing.

We ask peers to avoid excessive pre‐pending and de-aggregation where possible.

We expect peers to honour the ‘no-export’ BGP community sent by us.

Peers must agree never to statically route, or otherwise cause traffic, to flow towards any prefix we do not explicitly announce via BGP.

ZANOG will only peer via eBGP on public ASN’s, on public address space (we will not peer over RFC1918 address space or to a private ASN).

We expect peers to maintain a route set in a route registry of their choice, and have it listed in peeringdb, by which we will generate filters from

We expect the RPKI signing of all transmitted prefixes.

We expect peers to only announce prefixes that are legitimately assigned to them or their customers.

We expect peers to have sufficient capacity on their peering links to avoid congestion and reserve the right to de-peer any party who is consistently running congested peering circuits.

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.
• O MD5 não é necessário

data.notes:
A Multnet Telecom Ltda possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

data.name: Pemkot Bogor
data.notes:
Sejarah Bogor

Hampir secara umum penduduk Bogor mempunyai keyakinan bahwa Kota Bogor mempunyai hubungan lokatif dengan Kota Pakuan, ibukota Pajajaran. Asal-usul dan arti Pakuan terdapat dalam berbagai sumber. Di bawah ini adalah hasil penelusuran dari sumber-sumber tersebut berdasarkan urutan waktu:

Naskah Carita Waruga Guru (1750-an). Dalam naskah berbahasa Sunda Kuna ini diterangkan bahwa nama Pakuan Pajajaran didasarkan bahwa di lokasi tersebut banyak terdapat pohon Pakujajar.


K.F. Holle (1869). Dalam tulisan berjudul De Batoe Toelis te Buitenzorg (Batutulis di Bogor), Holle menyebutkan bahwa di dekat Kota Bogor terdapat kampung bernama Cipaku, beserta sungai yang memiliki nama yang sama. Di sana banyak ditemukan pohon paku. Jadi menurut Holle, nama Pakuan ada kaitannya dengan kehadiran Cipaku dan pohon paku. Pakuan Pajajaran berarti pohon paku yang berjajar ("op rijen staande pakoe bomen").

G.P. Rouffaer (1919) dalam Encyclopedie van Niederlandsch Indie edisi Stibbe tahun 1919. Pakuan mengandung pengertian "paku", akan tetapi harus diartikan "paku jagat" (spijker der wereld) yang melambangkan pribadi raja seperti pada gelar Paku Buwono dan Paku Alam. "Pakuan" menurut Fouffaer setara dengan "Maharaja". Kata "Pajajaran" diartikan sebagai "berdiri sejajar" atau "imbangan" (evenknie). Yang dimaksudkan Rouffaer adalah berdiri sejajar atau seimbang dengan Majapahit. Sekalipun Rouffaer tidak merangkumkan arti Pakuan Pajajaran, namun dari uraiannya dapat disimpulkan bahwa Pakuan Pajajaran menurut pendapatnya berarti "Maharaja yang berdiri sejajar atau seimbang dengan (Maharaja) Majapahit". Ia sependapat dengan Hoesein Djajaningrat (1913) bahwa Pakuan Pajajaran didirikan tahun 1433.


R. Ng. Poerbatjaraka (1921). Dalam tulisan De Batoe-Toelis bij Buitenzorg (Batutulis dekat Bogor) ia menjelaskan bahwa kata "Pakuan" mestinya berasal dari bahasa Jawa kuno "pakwwan" yang kemudian dieja "pakwan" (satu "w", ini tertulis pada Prasasti Batutulis). Dalam lidah orang Sunda kata itu akan diucapkan "pakuan". Kata "pakwan" berarti kemah atau istana. Jadi, Pakuan Pajajaran, menurut Poerbatjaraka, berarti "istana yang berjajar"(aanrijen staande hoven).

H. Ten Dam (1957). Sebagai Insinyur Pertanian, Ten Dam ingin meneliti kehidupan sosial-ekonomi petani Jawa Barat dengan pendekatan awal segi perkembangan sejarah. Dalam tulisannya, Verkenningen Rondom Padjadjaran (Pengenalan sekitar Pajajaran), pengertian "Pakuan" ada hubungannya dengan "lingga" (tonggak) batu yang terpancang di sebelah prasasti Batutulis sebagai tanda kekuasaan. Ia mengingatkan bahwa dalam Carita Parahyangan disebut-sebut tokoh Sang Haluwesi dan Sang Susuktunggal yang dianggapnya masih mempunyai pengertian "paku".


Ia berpendapat bahwa "pakuan" bukanlah nama, melainkan kata benda umum yang berarti ibukota (hoffstad) yang harus dibedakan dari keraton. Kata "pajajaran" ditinjaunya berdasarkan keadaan topografi. Ia merujuk laporan Kapiten Wikler (1690) yang memberitakan bahwa ia melintasi istana Pakuan di Pajajaran yang terletak antara Sungai Besar dengan Sungai Tanggerang (disebut juga Ciliwung dan Cisadane). Ten Dam menarik kesimpulan bahwa nama "Pajajaran" muncul karena untuk beberapa kilometer Ciliwung dan Cisadane mengalir sejajar. Jadi, Pakuan Pajajaran dalam pengertian Ten Dam adalah Pakuan di Pajajaran atau "Dayeuh Pajajaran".

Sebutan "Pakuan", "Pajajaran", dan "Pakuan Pajajaran" dapat ditemukan dalam Prasasti Batutulis (nomor 1 & 2) sedangkan nomor 3 bisa dijumpai pada Prasasti Kebantenan di Bekasi.


Dalam naskah Carita Parahiyangan ada kalimat berbunyi "Sang Susuktunggal, inyana nu nyieunna palangka Sriman Sriwacana Sri Baduga Maharajadiraja Ratu Haji di Pakwan Pajajaran nu mikadatwan Sri Bima Punta Narayana Madura Suradipati, inyana pakwan Sanghiyang Sri Ratu Dewata" (Sang Susuktunggal, dialah yang membuat tahta Sriman Sriwacana (untuk) Sri Baduga Maharaja Ratu Penguasa di Pakuan Pajajaran yang bersemayam di keraton Sri Bima Punta Narayana Madura Suradipati, yaitu pakuan Sanghiyang Sri Ratu Dewata).


Sanghiyang Sri Ratu Dewata adalah gelar lain untuk Sri Baduga. Jadi yang disebut "pakuan" itu adalah "kadaton" yang bernama Sri Bima dan seterunya. "Pakuan" adalah tempat tinggal untuk raja, biasa disebut keraton, kedaton atau istana. Jadi tafsiran Poerbatjaraka lah yang sejalan dengan arti yang dimaksud dalam Carita Parahiyangan, yaitu "istana yang berjajar". Tafsiran tersebut lebih mendekati lagi bila dilihat nama istana yang cukup panjang tetapi terdiri atas nama-nama yang berdiri sendiri. Diperkirakan ada lima (5) bangunan keraton yang masing-masing bernama: Bima, Punta, Narayana, Madura dan Suradipati. Inilah mungkin yang biasa disebut dalam peristilahan klasik "panca persada" (lima keraton). Suradipati adalah nama keraton induk. Hal ini dapat dibandingkan dengan nama-nama keraton lain, yaitu Surawisesa di Kawali, Surasowan di Banten dan Surakarta di Jayakarta pada masa silam.


Karena nama yang panjang itulah mungkin orang lebih senang meringkasnya, Pakuan Pajajaran atau Pakuan atau Pajajaran. Nama keraton dapat meluas menjadi nama ibukota dan akhirnya menjadi nama negara. Contohnya : Nama keraton Surakarta Hadiningrat dan Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat, yang meluas menjadi nama ibukota dan nama daerah. Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat dalam bahasa sehari-hari cukup disebut Yogya.


Pendapat Ten Dam (Pakuan = ibukota ) benar dalam penggunaan, tetapi salah dari segi semantik. Dalam laporan Tome Pires (1513) disebutkan bahwa bahwa ibukota kerajaan Sunda itu bernama "Dayo" (dayeuh) dan terletak di daerah pegunungan, dua hari perjalanan dari pelabuhan Kalapa di muara Ciliwung. Nama "Dayo" didengarnya dari penduduk atau pembesar Pelabuhan Kalapa. Jadi jelas, orang Pelabuhan Kalapa menggunakan kata "dayeuh" (bukan "pakuan") bila bermaksud menyebut ibukota. Dalam percakapan sehari-hari, digunakan kata "dayeuh", sedangkan dalam kesusastraan digunakan "pakuan" untuk menyebut ibukota kerajaan.

data.name: Roxonic Systems
data.notes:
## AS142289 - Roxonic Systems

*AS142289 is a non-commercial/not-for-profit research & development network based in India.*
***
### Routing policy & information:

#### Prefixes announced:

- 2a0e:46c4:106::/48
- 2a0e:46c4:2c10::/44
- 2a06:a005:700::/44
- 2a06:a005:a30::/44
- 2a06:a005:a40::/44
- 2a06:a005:a50::/44
- 2a06:a005:a60::/44
- 2a0e:b107:15f0::/44


***
### AS-SETs:

All AS-SETs of AS142289 are available in the RIPE IRRDB.

By default, all members of AS142289 should configure their network to allow advertisements from **AS-ROXONIC** AS-SET.

- **AS-ROXONIC** - *Contains AS142289 itself and its downstream members. This is the default AS-SET that members should use if they are using any IRRDB based filtering.*

- **AS-ROXONIC-UPSTREAMS** - *Contains only transit providers of AS142289.*

- **AS-ROXONIC-PEERS** - *Contains bilateral peering members of AS142289.*

- **AS-ROXONIC-RSPEERS** - *Contains route server/IX peering members of AS142289.*

- **AS-ROXONIC-DOWNSTREAMS** - *Contains only downstream members of AS142289.*


---

### BGP Large Communities:

We have implemented BGP large communities in our network. Currently, only informational communities are supported.

- **142289:1:0** - *Route received from an upstream member of AS142289.*

- **142289:2:0** - *Route received from an internet exchange.*

- **142289:3:0** - *Route received from a bilateral/private peering member of AS142289.*

- **142289:4:0** - *Route originated internally (This community is added by us when announcing prefixes owned by AS142289 to other members).*

- **142289:5:0** - *Route received from a downstream member of AS142289.*

Each and every member of Roxonic Systems will be tagged with a large community attribute, based on the nature of its relationship with AS142289.
For example, prefixes from an upstream provider whose ASN is 65530 will be tagged with: **142289:1:65530**


We are a MANRS compliant network. You can find more about our implemented actions by clicking [here](https://www.manrs.org/participant/3690/).

data.name: LACKNET SERVIÇOS DE TELECOMUNICAÇÕES
data.notes:
A INOVANET TELECOMUNICACOES E MULTIMIDIA LTDA possui uma política seletiva de peering, as sessões são estabelecidas com base no desempenho, capacidade e onde exista benefício mútuo e estão sujeitos a certos requisitos técnicos, comerciais e legais. Os requisitos técnicos gerais para peering são:

• Uma rede redundante com capacidade suficiente para troca de tráfego sem congestionamento ou lentidão.

• Um Centro de Operação de Rede (Network Operations Center – NOC) com experiência e qualificação, capaz de auxiliar na resolução de: o Todos os problemas técnicos de desempenho e configurações. o Todas as violações de segurança, ataques de negação de serviço ou qualquer outro abuso originado no peer ou seus clientes.

• Um ASN roteado publicamente.

• Pelo menos uma classe /24 roteada publicamente.

• Informações completas com o peeringdb.com

• Nenhuma das partes estabelecerá uma rota estática, uma rota de último recurso, ou de outra forma enviará tráfego para a outra parte por uma rota não anunciada via BGP.

• Comunicação suportada para os protocolos IPv4 e IPv6.

• Espera-se que ambas as partes registrem suas rotas em um banco de dados público de Internet Routing Registry (IRR), para fins de filtragem.

• Ambas as partes farão esforços de boa fé para manter essas informações atualizadas.

• O MD5 não é necessário

CGR - lacknettelecom@gmail.com

data.notes:
PIT DOMINICANO Route Servers - PEERING Policy

We operate three route servers (BIRDv2) across our sites, supporting RPKI and IRRdb filtering.

RS1: PIT-STI

RS2: PIT-BON

RS3: PIT-SDQ

Redundancy Requirement: For optimal routing, members are requested to peer with at least two (2) route servers.

A. Propagation Management (Large Communities)
Use these communities to control prefix propagation:

Do not advertise to specific AS: 64168:0:Destination_ASN

Advertise ONLY to specific AS: 64168:1:Destination_ASN

Do not advertise to anyone: 64168:0:0

Advertise to all (Default): 64168:1:0

B. Traffic Engineering (AS-PATH Prepend)
Influence inbound traffic by prepending your ASN:

Prepend to ALL: 64168:101:0 (1 hop), 64168:102:0 (2 hops), 64168:103:0 (3 hops)

Prepend to specific AS: 64168:101:ASN (1 hop), 64168:102:ASN (2 hops), 64168:103:ASN (3 hops)

C. Standard Filters (Legacy)
For legacy equipment compatibility:

Block specific AS: 0:ASN_Destination

Block all AS: 0:64168

Allow specific AS: 64168:ASN_Destination

data.name: Peravix
data.notes:
https://peravix.co.uk
Peravix delivers secure, scalable IT infrastructure with UK data residency, 24/7 expert support, and enterprise-grade security

--- AS204208 Peering Policy ---

Policy: Open
Contract: Not required (route server) / Required for bilateral
IPv4: Yes (min /24)
IPv6: Yes (min /48, dual-stack mandatory)
RS Peering: All route servers at all IXPs
Bilateral: Min 50 Mbps 95th% sustained over 30 days
Ratio: Up to 4:1 (bidirectional) for bilats; RS otherwise
MD5: Required on bilats
BFD: Required on bilats (300ms min interval)
Multilateral: Accepted via route servers

Requirements:
- Valid IRR objects (RPKI preferred); unrouted prefixes may be filtered
- Up-to-date PeeringDB record with NOC/abuse contacts
- 24-hour abuse response SLA
- No default routes or statics toward our prefixes
- No MED manipulation or community stripping
- No transit resale of our routes
- No hijacked or disputed prefixes

We reserve the right to de-peer without notice for route leaks,
prefix hijacking, persistent abuse, or sustained ratio violations.

Contact: noc@peravix.co.uk
